status: Accepted engine work complete; reusable construction scratch trial rejected, no new contiguous vector layout or startup checkpoint implemented.
source_baseline: Same native Windows checkout before immutable RecordMap and CRC/replay changes, based on HEAD 62e2902. Optional internal group fields do not affect the default-feature benchmark.
api: crate-private Database::durable_group<T>(FnOnce(&mut Self)->T)->Result<T>; server owns owner-lock discipline and sends no provisional success before outer Ok
semantics: O(1) immutable generation capture; COW ID tree on first following write, immutable Arc<Record> bodies share unchanged vectors/payloads/metadata; public Record unchanged.
At most 8 distinct read captures per Database, each <=100000 physical records and <=128MiB logical body bytes; clones share one lease; no hidden retained-version registry.
Default snapshot TTL frozen at capture time; explicit _at APIs available.
Background unquantized capture shares records with total retained logical body cap256MiB, in addition to configured vector/record limits; ScalarU8 still trains/encodes synchronously.
Publication rejects worker when collection vector version is not covered by bounded catchup.

Group callback results are provisional, not externally committed until final sync. Validation rejects remain per-frame. Append/final-sync errors poison; callback unwind resets scope and poisons before resume. Group is NOT one transaction and does NOT roll back valid neighboring frames.
commands: cargo test --lib --test read_snapshots --test background_hnsw --test ann_snapshot --test snapshot_lifecycle_boundaries --test batches --test encryption --test format_v5 --test hnsw_maintenance --test metrics --test conditional --test replica --test named_vectors --test metadata_index --test hybrid --quiet
limitations: Warm-cache bounded synthetic 2048x512 data, 11 capture and21 reopen samples; shared host, not production throughput/latency guarantees.
Read snapshots are exact/browse/get only, no derived ANN/text/metadata/sparse/disk/GPU indexes. Server uses snapshots only on simple unindexed exact/no-rerank path, with explicit fallback at limits.
First writer may still copy O(n) ID tree; this is not lock-free persistent-tree MVCC. Modified metadata can copy that record vector/payload while old generation is retained.
Shared rebuild retains complete immutable record bodies, hence the new256MiB retention cap. This can reject payload-heavy collections that fit vector-only limits.
Slicing8 CRC and borrowed/reusable verified replay frame buffers accepted; no on-disk format/checksum changes, no checkpoint. Decoding itself remains same, profiled at~2ms per4MiB.

Reusable HNSW construction scratch and reusable result buffer prototyped; six paired9-trial campaigns had mixed wins/regressions and no reliable gain, so all candidate scratch code/tests removed. Existing prior selected-vector cache preserved. No new contiguous vector layout implemented.

memory_and_locality_tradeoff.representation_before: BTreeMap<u64, Record>; Record inline in B-tree, Vec data separately allocated.
memory_and_locality_tradeoff.representation_after: Arc<BTreeMap<u64, Arc<Record>>>; one new Arc allocation and pointer indirection per record, Vec data still separately allocated.
memory_and_locality_tradeoff.unconditional_cost: Applies even when no read snapshot or rebuild is active: per-record allocation at put/replay, extra record pointer dereference in scans/ANN lookups; vectors are NOT newly contiguous.
memory_and_locality_tradeoff.nominal_increment_derivation: Two pointer-sized strong/weak counts (16 bytes) plus one pointer stored in tree (8 bytes), because inline Record bytes move from tree to Arc allocation. Ignores allocator bookkeeping/alignment and B-tree capacity/padding effects; not an RSS measurement.
memory_and_locality_tradeoff.measurement_limitations: No allocator/RSS comparison was performed. Do not claim total-memory reduction or locality improvement. Small vectors and metadata-heavy workloads may regress despite the 512-dimensional benchmark gains.
memory_and_locality_tradeoff.reopen_tradeoff: Replay reconstructs an additional Arc allocation for each live record, although repeated updates replace/drop prior Arc values. Observed final reopen gain combines compatible CRC acceleration and borrowed/reused frame buffers with this allocation regression; no isolated Arc reconstruction speedup is claimed.
memory_and_locality_tradeoff.retention_tradeoff: O(1) capture avoids deep vector/payload/metadata copy; first write while retained clones O(n) ID tree and increments shared record references. Superseded record bodies persist until last snapshot/job reference drops. Logical retention caps exclude allocator overhead/current live database.
memory_and_locality_tradeoff.reusable_hnsw_scratch: Rejected/reverted: mixed paired measurements, no reliable gain.
memory_and_locality_tradeoff.checkpoint: Not added: measured compatible CRC/replay-buffer improvements addressed profiled bottleneck without format or recovery changes.

integration_note: This measurement-time artifact predates final integration. A concurrent, unpublished graph OpenAPI baseline initially failed; that baseline was subsequently reconciled. The later unfiltered workspace validation passed 458 tests with 4 ignored. Graph changes are not part of this optimization publication; historical measurement logs are not a current CI-status report.

mixed_workload_followup.scope: Same-engine lock-held vs snapshot read scans with concurrent durable writes, correctness assertions, separate warmed first-write COW pairs. Not a pre-Arc baseline.
mixed_workload_followup.summary: Median writer lock wait0.710ms->0.0002ms, durable write1.221ms->0.828ms; reader total0.729ms->0.903ms (regression). In-memory first-write unique0.002ms vs retained0.124ms. Snapshot write max14.523ms vs lock-held2.838ms. No universal speedup claim.
